newsitem.title: NORWAY: Coastguard begins attempts to free stranded liner.
newsitem.headline: Coastguard begins attempts to free stranded liner.

text.p: Norwegian rescue services have begun operations to free a cruise liner stranded on rocks and sand off the Arctic island of Spitzbergen, an official said on Tuesday.

Kaare Oyre, controller at the rescue centre for northern Norway at Bodoe, said coastguards planned to unload at least part of the ship's 480 tonne cargo of heavy fuel oil before attempting to drag her free.

"There are three coastguard ships at the site. One will pump off at least part of the oil, which should take four to five hours," he told Reuters. "The other two will try and tow her free afterwards."

The 9,000 deadweight tonne Bahamian-resgistered Hanseatic, carrying 145 mainly German tourists and a crew of 115, ran aground on Sunday in the Hinlopen fjord off Spitzbergen's north coast. It was on its way from Norway to Iceland via the scenic island.
There were no injuries and the liner's owners, Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd AG, said an inspection of the hull by divers had found only minor damage.

Oyre said all passengers and crew would remain aboard the Hanseatic. However, there were contingency plans to evacuate the ship if the wind changed to a northerly direction because of a danger of a build-up of ice in the area.
The Hanseatic also ran aground last August. The same captain hit a sandbank on a voyage in northwest Canada, ending the boat's tour through the Arctic for the 268 people on board.
